county.name: Kim Louise Lemoine
county.subject: Counterfeit government checks / identity theft
county.amountType: Counterfeit-check total described by California DOJ
county.outcome: California DOJ reported guilty pleas in Sonoma Superior Court to identity theft, forgery and grand theft and a five-year prison sentence.
county.details: The state Attorney General's sentencing announcement and a filed Sonoma court complaint provide government documentation. The complaint itself describes initial charges; the press release supplies the later conviction and sentence. The supplied portal docket records a May 8, 2012 restitution determination of $301,528.18 jointly and severally with co-defendants, and minutes for April 30, 2015 report that an expungement motion was denied with outstanding restitution noted. Those entries do not establish the balance today or whether any subsequent relief occurred. The July 8, 2009 sentencing minutes also state restitution of $302,361 jointly and severally to Bank of America; this differs from the May 8, 2012 restitution determination of $301,528.18 jointly with co-defendants. The printout does not clarify how these recorded amounts relate or establish a current balance. The July 8 2009 sentencing minutes on source page 28 specify a five-year aggregate state-prison term whose execution was suspended, with commitment to the California Rehabilitation Center for up to five years. The five-year term should not be presented as five years actually served in state prison.
county.courtRecordStatus: 35-page matching court portal printout visually triaged page by page November 22, 2026. Source pp28 and 33–35 support distinct 2009 and 2012 restitution entries and a 2015 denied expungement motion. Record includes medical/psychological evaluation and personal-detail references; full original withheld pending detailed redaction. Only header excerpt published.
